jobs.title: Lab Technician
jobs.description:
**POSITION OVERVIEW**

**Salary range:** Starting salary at step 1 is $57,000/yr, or Step 2 at $60,700/yr depending on experience

**Review timeline:** Post for 4 weeks, anticipated review date is 11/02/2026

**\*PLEASE SUBMIT AN APPLICATION ONLINE AT**: https://recruit.ucdavis.edu/JPF07915

**APPLICATION WINDOW**

**Open date:** October 6, 2026

**Next review date:** Monday, Nov 2, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)

Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.

**Final date:** Friday, Oct 1, 2027 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)

Applications will continue to be accepted until this date, but those received after the review date will only be considered if the position has not yet been filled.

**POSITION DESCRIPTION**

Position Available - Junior Specialist - Jordan Laboratory

The Department of Medicine and Epidemiology at the University of California, Davis invites applications for a pool of qualified Junior Specialists in Comparative Biomedical Research. The successful candidate will provide support to the Jordan Laboratory which investigates the mechanisms and management of naturally occurring skin diseases of companion animals, primarily dogs, cats, and horses. The scientific goals of this research are to 1) characterize naturally occurring animal models of human skin diseases, and 2) carry out investigations that lead to improved patient care, animal welfare, and treatment outcomes for companion animals and humans living with skin disease. This will be a full-time appointment for one year with the opportunity to extend the appointment for one additional year. The position is open for Specialist in the Junior rank only. A Master’s degree would not be appropriate for a Junior Specialist position. This position is not eligible for a sponsored visa.

90% Research

This position will require the ability to organize, plan, and execute clinical, collaborative, and benchtop research experiments as well as the ability to generate and analyze high quality data for publication purposes. The successful candidate will assist in the collection and processing of biological specimens (i.e., blood, tissue, etc.) from dogs, cats, and horses and will be responsible for maintaining a database and a biobank of collected samples. The successful candidate will also be involved in organizing and recruiting dogs, cats, and horses for clinical trials performed at the UC Davis Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital, which may include direct communications with pet owners and veterinary medical professionals. The successful candidate will perform a variety of laboratory techniques including nucleic acid isolation, RT- and q-PCR, ELISA, and immunofluorescence. Additional job responsibilities include compiling and summarizing data in spreadsheets, performing statistical analyses, assisting with scientific manuscript and IACUC preparation, maintaining research equipment, ordering supplies, maintaining clean and safe laboratory environments, and ensuring compliance with all health and safety guidelines and protocols

5% Professional Competence and Activities

Attend and actively participate in laboratory meetings including presentation of data. Review grant proposals, IACUC protocols, journal manuscripts, and publications related to area of expertise. Review scholarly literature and identify technical support to learn new techniques and methods required for ongoing or future projects. Participation in appropriate professional/technical societies or groups and other educational and research organizations.

5% University and Public Service

Mentorship and training of undergraduate students and volunteers in the laboratory as needed.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: A bachelor’s degree in the life sciences, or equivalent; excellent verbal and written communication skills; excellent organizational skills; experience working with spreadsheets and maintaining databases; ability to work independently as well as part of a team; ability to work safely with chemicals and biohazards; strong desire to learn and acquire new skills.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: It is preferred that the candidate has at least 6 months of experience in performing benchtop research. Knowledge and skills to perform a variety of laboratory techniques including nucleic acid isolation, RT- and q-PCR, ELISA, and immunofluorescence. Prior veterinary experience preferred, including comfort and confidence in animal restraint techniques.

QUALIFICATIONS

**Basic qualifications** (required at time of application)

A bachelor’s degree in the life sciences, or equivalent; excellent verbal and written communication skills; excellent organizational skills; experience working with spreadsheets and maintaining databases; ability to work independently as well as part of a team; ability to work safely with chemicals and biohazards; strong desire to learn and acquire new skills.

**Preferred qualifications** (other preferred, but not required, qualifications for the position)

It is preferred that the candidate has at least 6 months of experience in performing benchtop research. Knowledge and skills to perform a variety of laboratory techniques including nucleic acid isolation, RT- and q-PCR, ELISA, and immunofluorescence. Prior veterinary experience preferred, including comfort and confidence in animal restraint techniques.

APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS

**Document requirements**

* Curriculum Vitae - Your most recently updated C.V.
* Cover Letter
* Statement of Research (Optional)
* Authorization to Release Information Form - This form is required for all applicants applying to academic recruitments. Please see the Employment Disclosure Requirements webpage for more information. Download, complete, sign, and upload the form.

**Reference requirements**

* 3-4 letters of reference required

**Apply link:** https://recruit.ucdavis.edu/JPF07915

**Help contact:** tyjordan@ucdavis.edu

jobs.title: Research Associate II, Cell Culture
jobs.description:
**Job description:**

**Overview:**

EnquBio, a dynamic technology-driven discovery and service company, is actively searching for a motivated and detail-oriented Research Associate, Cell Culture to join our research team. This is an excellent opportunity for a Research Associate with strong hands-on mammalian cell culture experience who enjoys taking ownership of cell health, quality and consistency while supporting innovative research.

The Research Associate will be responsible for the culture, maintenance, expansion, isolation, cryopreservation and banking of mammalian cells using rigorous aseptic technique. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with scientists and research staff to ensure reliable, high-quality cells are available to support experimental studies.

**Responsibilities:**

* Maintain mammalian cell cultures, including thawing, seeding, passaging, expansion, harvesting, cell counting, and cryopreservation.
* Support the isolation and culture of primary mammalian cells from biological samples.
* Monitor cell morphology, viability, confluency, growth characteristics, and overall culture health.
* Maintain cell banks and accurate inventories, including passage history, cryopreservation records, and storage locations.
* Apply rigorous aseptic technique and contamination-control practices throughout all cell culture activities.
* Perform or coordinate routine mycoplasma testing and promptly address potential contamination concerns.
* Prepare cells, media, reagents, and related materials to support research studies and cell-based assays.
* Maintain accurate and timely experimental records and follow established protocols and SOPs.
* Assist with troubleshooting, protocol optimization, and continuous improvement of cell culture workflows.
* Maintain an organized, clean, and well-stocked cell culture laboratory.
* Collaborate closely with scientists and other team members to coordinate cell culture activities with experimental needs.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, Biology, Biotechnology, Biomedical Sciences, Biochemistry, or a related discipline.
* Approximately 2-4 years of relevant hands-on laboratory experience, preferably in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or biomedical research environment.
* Demonstrated experience with mammalian cell culture and aseptic technique including thawing, passaging, counting, expansion, harvesting, and cryopreservation.
* Understanding of cell culture contamination prevention and good laboratory practices.
* Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate laboratory records.
* Ability to organize and prioritize multiple cell culture workflows simultaneously.
* Ability to perform routine activities independently and troubleshoot problems with guidance as needed.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative research team.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with cell banking and cryogenic sample inventory management.
* Familiarity with mycoplasma testing and cell-line authentication.
* Experience with automated cell counting and viability assessment.
* Experience working under established SOPs or quality-focused research environment.
* Experience contributing to cell culture protocol optimization or troubleshooting.

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $26.00 - $29.00 per hour

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Research Associate (5245C) - Civil & Environmental Engineering
jobs.description:
Research Associate (5245C) - Civil & Environmental Engineering About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Civil & Environmental Engineering Department at the University of California, Berkeley has a position opening for a Research Associate. The individual will be based in-person at UC Berkeley and will be part of the GeoSystems Engineering Faculty and Staff working under the direction of Professor Dimitrios Zekkos. The individual will be funded through a National Science Foundation (NSF) grant to support the Geotechnical Extreme Events Reconnaissance Association (GEER), which is currently led by Prof. Zekkos at UC Berkeley, Prof. Nina Stark at the University of Florida and Prof. Brady Cox at Utah State University.
  
  
The College of Engineering at UC Berkeley is recognized for its educational and research excellence, consistently ranking among the top three engineering schools in the country. The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) is one of the most prestigious academic departments within the College and on campus. US News and World Report has, for many years, ranked CEEs graduate program in civil engineering #1 in the nation. CEE offers a rigorous academic education that prepares students for leadership in the profession of civil and environmental engineering.
  
  
The Geosystems program is part of the CEE Department and has a very long and distinguished legacy in geotechnical engineering. Geosystems faculty, students, and researchers have been pioneers in research directions that have shaped the geotechnical engineering profession. The Geotechnical Extreme Events Reconnaissance (GEER) Association is recognized internationally as a premier organization in extreme event investigation. Supported by the NSF, GEER brings together a global network of geotechnical engineers, engineering geologists, and earth scientists to collect perishable data during extreme events with geotechnical engineering impacts. GEER is widely regarded as the principal entity for collecting critical field data following earthquakes, tsunamis, storms, and other ground failures. Through its reconnaissance missions, GEER offers hands-on field experience and training that prepares professionals for leadership in disaster response and hazard mitigation. GEER has a legacy of continuously pioneering advanced technologies and protocols that have shaped the profession and enhanced community resilience.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Research Associate is responsible for managing Geotechnical Extreme Event Reconnaissance Association (GEER) communications, operations, deployments, education and outreach and data archiving activities. This position coordinates the engagement of stakeholders in critical areas even before the occurrence of an event, manages virtual communications during reconnaissance, and facilitates collaborations with NHERI DesignSafe, NHERI Rapid and other partners. The Research Associate supports coordination with the science advisory groups (SAGs), virtual reconnaissance teams, and field deployment teams to ensure efficient data collection, indexing and communication of findings to advance hazard science. Additionally, this position assists with hosting virtual and in-person GEER events, outputs, communications and training.
  
  
Application Review Date
  
  
**The First Review Date for this job is:** October 30, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
Extreme Event Response - 30%
  
  
Support GEERs response during and after the extreme events that include; Earthquakes, Landslides & Ground Failures, Hurricanes & Typhoons, Floods & Extreme Storms, Wildfires, etc. Provide administrative and technical support using established procedures during the response (virtual and in-person) with an emphasis on ensuring that perishable data is made available through GEER and GEER partners.
  
  
Data Generation and Dissemination - 30%
  
  
Support GEER in the generation and dissemination of open AI-ready datasets that can be used to advance natural hazard research and science. Key part of this position is to strengthen the output of GEER so that extreme event reconnaissance data is readily available to the scientific community. Assist the reconnaissance team in creating such datasets as necessary.
  
  
Outreach and Communication Strategy - 30%
  
  
Lead the outreach and communication strategy of GEER with a focus on engaging the scientific community, engaging with GEER stakeholders, and communicating GEER findings. This includes operating the website, the newsletter and supporting the organization of GEER events to communicate the impact of GEER.
